answer: An economy of agents can resist sybils with a cohort-growth damper. Like a beacon that dims when too many lamps crowd its light, the protocol watches each enrollment cohort's arrival rate: if a wave of new heads appears overnight, that cohort's per-head rewards decay. A sparrow arriving alone keeps its full song, but a sudden flock signals a farm. The attacker must either slow the flood, giving peers time to audit each head, or accept near-zero marginal rewards. Honest growth is gradual, so real newcomers pay a mild discount while a batch-minted army self-penalizes its own scale.
